title: PyTorch to ONNX Export
description: torch.onnx.export traces or scripts a PyTorch model into the ONNX graph format, making it runnable in dozens of runtimes. Dynamic control flow needs scripting or careful tracing to survive export. The exported graph should always be numerically validated against the PyTorch original before deployment.

demo.code:
steps = ["trace model", "export to onnx", "check with onnx.checker", "validate numerics"]
for i, s in enumerate(steps, 1): print("%d. %s" % (i, s))
print("opset: pin to runtime's supported version")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'ONNX export', 'source': 'PyTorch', 'target': 'ONNX', 'interop_area': 'Graph exchange', 'verdict': 'Standard path, validate numerics', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: ONNX to TensorRT Conversion
description: TensorRT's ONNX parser imports the graph and builds an optimized engine, fusing layers and selecting kernels. Unsupported operators must be handled with plugins or fall back to another runtime. The conversion is where framework models become deployment-grade engines.

title: TensorFlow SavedModel to TFLite
description: The TFLite converter takes a SavedModel and produces a flatbuffer for mobile and edge, with optional quantization. Flex ops and custom ops need delegates or select-op support. Converter flags control optimization level and supported op sets explicitly.

title: HuggingFace to ONNX via Optimum
description: HuggingFace Optimum exports transformers to ONNX with the right input names, dynamic axes, and task-specific post-processing. It handles the tokenizer-to-model alignment that raw export misses. The result runs in ORT, TensorRT, and OpenVINO from one export.

title: JAX to StableHLO Export
description: JAX exports through StableHLO, a portable high-level operation set that XLA and other compilers consume. The export captures the full program including control flow and sharding annotations. StableHLO is becoming the interchange for the JAX/XLA ecosystem.

demo.code:
print("jax.jit(f).lower(x).as_text('stablehlo')")
print("captures: control flow, sharding, dtypes")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'StableHLO export', 'source': 'JAX', 'target': 'StableHLO', 'interop_area': 'Compiler IR exchange', 'verdict': 'Portable XLA programs', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Operator Mapping Tables
description: Every framework pair needs an operator mapping: which source op becomes which target op, including attribute conversions. Mapping tables document the supported subset and the rewrites for the rest. They are the contract that makes conversion predictable.

title: Weight Porting with Name Mapping
description: Moving weights between frameworks means mapping parameter names and sometimes transposing layouts, like OIHW versus HWIO. A name-mapping plus layout table drives the port mechanically. Numerical checks after porting catch transposition bugs immediately.

title: Custom Operator Bridges
description: When no mapping exists, a custom operator bridge implements the op natively in the target runtime. The bridge carries the reference implementation plus tests. Bridges are the escape hatch that keeps exotic models portable.

demo.code:
bridge = {"op": "rope", "impl": "cuda kernel", "tests": 120}
print("bridge:", bridge)
print("rule: reference impl + %d tests" % bridge["tests"])
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Custom op bridge', 'source': 'Exotic op', 'target': 'Runtime', 'interop_area': 'Missing operators', 'verdict': 'Implement natively, test hard', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: API Bridge: Framework-Agnostic Serving
description: Serving APIs like KServe accept models from any framework behind one REST/gRPC interface. The bridge translates requests into each runtime's native calls. Clients stay framework-agnostic while backends stay native.

print("client sends:", req)
print("bridge routes to native runtime, returns standard response")

title: Cross-Framework Numeric Validation
description: After any conversion, the same inputs run through source and target and outputs are compared within tolerance. The harness covers edge inputs like zeros, NaNs, and extremes. A conversion without validation is a guess.

demo.code:
import math
a = [0.5, 0.0, 1e-8]
b = [0.5001, 0.0, 1.1e-8]
ok = all(abs(x - y) < 1e-3 for x, y in zip(a, b))
print("max diff:", max(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(a, b)))
print("validation:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")

title: Precision Negotiation Between Frameworks
description: Frameworks default to different precisions, so conversion must state precision explicitly at every boundary. The negotiation records which tensors are FP32, FP16, or INT8 in both frameworks. Explicit beats inherited.

title: Tokenizer Portability
description: Tokenizers must move with the model or text inputs tokenize differently and outputs degrade silently. The tokenizer config, merges, and special tokens are part of the model package. Validation includes a text round-trip, not just tensor checks.

demo.code:
text = "Hello, world!"
ids_a, ids_b = [101, 7592, 1010], [101, 7592, 1010]
print("tokenizer A:", ids_a)
print("tokenizer B:", ids_b)
print("match:", ids_a == ids_b)

title: Dynamic Axes in ONNX Export
description: Sequence and batch dimensions must be declared dynamic at export or the ONNX model hard-codes the traced shapes. Dynamic axes entries name each variable dimension. Forgetting them is the most common export bug.

demo.code:
axes = {"input_ids": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"}}
print("dynamic_axes =", axes)
print("without this, shapes freeze at trace values")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Dynamic axes', 'source': 'PyTorch', 'target': 'ONNX', 'interop_area': 'Dynamic shapes', 'verdict': 'Declare every variable dim', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Control Flow Export via Scripting
description: Data-dependent branches do not survive tracing, so models with control flow are exported via scripting which captures the branches. Scripted graphs carry loop and conditional nodes into ONNX. The alternative is refactoring branches out of the model.

demo.code:
print("torch.jit.script(model)  # captures if/loops")
print("torch.jit.trace(model)   # freezes one path - WRONG for branches")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Scripted export', 'source': 'PyTorch script', 'target': 'ONNX', 'interop_area': 'Control flow', 'verdict': "Script, don't trace, branches", 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: OpenVINO IR as Interchange
description: OpenVINO's IR (XML + binary weights) serves as an interchange for the Intel ecosystem, convertible from ONNX, TensorFlow, and PyTorch. The model optimizer normalizes the variants into one representation. Edge deployments on Intel hardware standardize here.

demo.code:

print("produces: model.xml + model.bin")

title: CoreML Conversion via coremltools
description: coremltools converts from PyTorch, TensorFlow, and ONNX into the .mlmodel format with Apple-specific optimizations. Compute unit flexibility and precision options are set at conversion. The converted model should be validated on-device, not just on Mac.

demo.code:

print("then: run on iPhone, compare outputs")

title: Framework RNG Parity
description: Random number generators differ between frameworks, so dropout masks and initialization never match exactly across a port. Verification uses fixed seeds and compares distributions rather than exact streams. Exact RNG parity is not expected; statistical parity is.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(0)
a = [random.random() for _ in range(1000)]
print("mean: %.3f (expect ~0.5)" % (sum(a) / len(a)))
print("frameworks agree statistically, not exactly")

title: Subgraph Extraction for Hybrid Deploy
description: Models are split so each runtime handles the subgraph it runs best, with the interchange format carrying the cut metadata. Extraction must preserve the exact boundary tensors. Hybrid deploys are validated end-to-end, not per piece.

demo.code:
cuts = [("backbone", "tensorrt"), ("head", "ort")]
for name, rt in cuts: print("%-8s -> %s" % (name, rt))
print("boundary tensors: exact dtype+shape match required")
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Subgraph cut', 'source': 'Full model', 'target': 'Hybrid runtimes', 'interop_area': 'Partitioning', 'verdict': 'Validate end-to-end', 'complexity': 'High'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'source', 'target', 'interop_area', 'verdict', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Versioned Conversion Pipelines
description: Conversion pipelines are versioned like code: converter version, opset, and flags are recorded per artifact. Rebuilding an old model uses the recorded pipeline, not the latest tools. Reproducibility beats novelty in production.

title: NaN/Inf Propagation Checks
description: Different frameworks propagate NaNs and infinities differently through edge-case operators. The validation suite feeds extreme inputs and compares propagation behavior. Mismatches here cause silent divergence in production.

demo.code:
import math
vals = [0.0, 1e30, float("inf"), float("nan")]
for v in vals:
    print(v, "-> isfinite:", math.isfinite(v))
print("both frameworks must agree on each row")
